clue.text: Present you send me less?

parts.note: read as a plea: be present with me less often and my love will grow, the old proverb about separation

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the gifts arriving from a partner have shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it means being there in person: send me less of your presence, and the proverb says I will love you more.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that being apart from someone makes you love them more, so asking to see them less is its joke.

clue.text: Like taking off gear at night — that includes gaudy tops

indicators.note: tops means the first letter of each of the words that come before it in the clue

explanation.surface: A remark that undressing at night must involve shedding loud, showy shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' looks like undressing, but it is an aircraft's take-off: an anti-g suit is worn by pilots against acceleration forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-g suits are flying kit that protects pilots from the strain of acceleration during take-off and manoeuvres.

clue.text: Dog in trap fought invisible opponent

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or shadow them
something held in a trap is boxed in

explanation.surface: A dog caught in a trap lashes out at an enemy nobody can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow-boxing is sparring against an imaginary opponent, as boxers do in training.

clue.text: Bond taking cue from agent holding firm in Belfast?

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
a gel is a setting agent that makes a liquid hold firm

explanation.surface: A spy picks up instructions from a contact sheltering inside a Belfast company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'agent' suggest James Bond, but this Bond takes a snooker cue: the professional player Nigel Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Bond is an English professional snooker player, so this Bond picks up a cue.

clue.text: One town some see as two, oddly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A single town that some people strangely perceive as two.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastwood is a town in Nottinghamshire, birthplace of D H Lawrence.

clue.text: Scrap fines, breaking into a beam

indicators.note: the fines break into the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: a beam of light is a ray
F is the abbreviation for fine, so two fines give FF

explanation.surface: Someone scraps penalties for burglary, here pictured as breaking into a light beam.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl, a scrap or fight.

clue.text: European Parliament and UN asked to work with Trade union leaders

indicators.note: to work means these letters are set working, rearranged into a new order
leaders means the first letters of trade and union

explanation.surface: Brussels and the United Nations are invited to cooperate with trade unions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Parliament' suggests Strasbourg, but it means any parliament in Europe: Finland's is the EDUSKUNTA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eduskunta is the national legislature of Finland, a parliament within Europe.

clue.text: Old portal refurbished for good money

indicators.note: refurbished means the letters of the two words are done up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An ancient doorway, restored, sells for a high price.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dollar is an idiom for the highest price, very good pay.

clue.text: Lyon's inside left stops keepers dominating people

parts.note: in French, the language of Lyon, en means in or inside

indicators.note: the letter for left stops up the other word, placed inside it

parts.note: people who keep money are savers

explanation.surface: A footballer playing inside left for Lyon blocks the goalkeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside left' looks like a football position; 'inside' belongs with Lyon, giving the French EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enslavers hold others in bondage, so they are people who dominate others.

clue.text: I'm for streaming pupils to bring order

definitions.text: I'm for streaming pupils to bring order

parts.words: I'm for streaming pupils to bring order
parts.note: spoken by a riot-control weapon that makes eyes water, the pupils of the eyes, to restore order

explanation.surface: A teacher claims to favour setting schoolchildren by ability for discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaming pupils' looks like grouping schoolchildren by ability, but it is weeping eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use a gas that makes the eyes water to disperse rioting crowds and restore order.

clue.text: Slip quickly, briefly, around to the French Windows

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the other pieces, enclosing them
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: quickly means fast
au is French for to the
XP is a version of Microsoft Windows

explanation.surface: Someone slips quickly out to the French windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Windows' looks like a pair of glass doors, but the words split: the French phrase for 'to the', then a Microsoft operating system.
explanation.definitionFit: A faux pas is a social blunder, a slip in manners.

clue.text: Turn and stare at Western journalist becoming one-hit wonder

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
to ogle is to stare at lecherously
a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter turns and gawps at a western news hack who has a single hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-hit wonder' suggests a pop act, but here it is a web search phrase returning exactly one result.
explanation.definitionFit: A googlewhack is a two-word search query that returns just a single page of results.

clue.text: One supplying lift to Bristol even from Aberfan

indicators.note: even means the second, fourth and sixth letters are picked from the word

explanation.surface: Someone provides a car ride to Bristol all the way from Aberfan, a Welsh village.
explanation.walkthrough: BRISTOLS is British rhyming slang for breasts (from Bristol City), so a garment lifts them. Aberfan is a village in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is underwear that supports and lifts the breasts.

clue.text: Litter round the house Rex put in order

indicators.note: put in means the king's letter is placed inside the rest
the brood goes round the other words, enclosing them

parts.note: a litter of young animals is a brood
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A pet owner tidies up the kittens' mess around the house that the dog Rex made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' looks like the anagram signal, but 'put in' inserts R and 'order' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious or fraternal order is a brotherhood of members bound by common rules.

clue.text: Bye bye, Prime Minister: inwardly nothing changes!

definitions.note: change-ringing in bells; the answer is one method of such changes

indicators.note: inwardly means the zero goes inside the two letters

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bye
B again, the cricket abbreviation for bye
nothing is zero, the letter O
John Major was British Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997

explanation.surface: A farewell to a Prime Minister, lamenting that nothing really changes under him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' sounds like politics, but it is bell-ringing: a method on eight bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Major is a method of change-ringing on eight bells, one sequence of changes.

clue.text: Orchestra and hosts performed ultimately in broadcasting capacity

parts.note: an orchestra is a band

indicators.note: hosts means the word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: with can mean and, as in 'bread with butter'

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of performed

explanation.surface: An orchestra and its hosts finally perform over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies, hence the data capacity, a transmission channel can carry.

clue.text: Paper supporting a new tax thwarting crime

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: a tithe is a tenth paid as a tax to the church
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper backs a new tax that would reduce crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-theft devices are designed to prevent stealing, so they thwart crime.

clue.text: Team bidding to escape slowly drop off

parts.note: in bridge, South and North bid as one partnership
liquid that escapes slowly oozes out

explanation.surface: A team bidding to slip away quietly lets the effort drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team bidding' sounds like a takeover attempt, but it is a bridge partnership, South and North.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep, briefly to doze.

clue.text: Face down overwhelming suspicion in West End bar

indicators.note: overwhelming means the other pieces swallow up the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a clock face is a dial

indicators.note: the west end of a word written left to right is its first letter

parts.note: feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: A drinker stares down suspicion in a West End pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but means the left-hand, first letter of 'suspicion'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to prohibit it, to refuse to allow it.

clue.text: Almost steers round the outside of tight turns

indicators.note: turns means the whole assembled piece is read backwards
the cattle go round the outer letters, enclosing them

parts.note: steers are bullocks, cattle, so oxen

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A driver nearly steers round the outer edge of a hairpin bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to can mean nearly, as in 'next to nothing', so it means almost.

clue.text: "Finnish" strippers, first class, managed tricks

parts.note: in Scottish schools P1, primary one, is the first class, with 1 read as I
to manage a business is to run it, so managed is ran
to have someone is to trick them, so has means tricks

explanation.surface: Finnish strippers in a first-class show managed some tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finnish' in quotes is a pun on finny-ish: fish that strip flesh from bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranhas are flesh-eating fish that can strip a carcass to the bone.

clue.text: See 7
Packet ships east off Virginia

indicators.note: ships means sends away, so a letter is sent off from the name
off means the letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Virginia Wade is a British tennis player who won Wimbledon in 1977

explanation.surface: A mail boat sails east from the coast of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like the American state, but it is the tennis player Virginia Wade.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet can mean a large sum of money, and a wad is a thick roll of banknotes.

clue.text: Skirmishing to John's rear for the present in war

indicators.note: skirmishing suggests a confused scuffle, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Fighting reaches the back of John's position as a gift in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'present' was the hollow wooden horse the Greeks left at Troy, hiding soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks gave Troy a wooden horse as a gift, hiding soldiers inside to take the city.

clue.text: Welcome United leaving Old Trafford turf to their fans?

indicators.note: leaving means the word for united is taken out

parts.words: Old Trafford turf to their fans
parts.note: Old Trafford is Manchester United's stadium, whose fans call it hallowed turf, sacred ground
wed means united, as in marriage

explanation.surface: Manchester United quit Old Trafford, a pitch their supporters hold sacred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club but means WED, joined in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is a greeting, a way of welcoming someone.

clue.text: Puzzle's not beginning to become smoother

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle

explanation.surface: A puzzle that loses its opening becomes easier going.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eases difficulties smooths them, so an easer is a smoother.

clue.text: Naturalist caller rudely rings back

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read backwards
the two words ring the run of letters, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A naturalist's rude caller keeps phoning back.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Durrell was a British naturalist, zookeeper and author of My Family and Other Animals.

clue.text: Valley flooded, breeze having got up

indicators.note: in a down answer, got up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a breeze is moving air

explanation.surface: A breeze has risen over a flooded valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley.

clue.text: Circuits have lines within bounds

indicators.note: within means the lines sit inside the circuits

parts.note: circuits are loops
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: Racing circuits have lines painted within their boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move in clumsy bounds, as a rabbit or big dog does.

clue.text: See 1
